literal: Whenever the imperial carriage went on tour, You often remained at Ye.
idiomatic: Whenever the emperor went on tour, You often remained at Ye.

literal: In the third month of the third year of Heqing, several dozen bandits including Tian Zili plotted to seize You as their leader; falsely claiming to be envoys, they went straight to You's residence, entered the inner chamber, declared an edict, dragged You onto a horse, threatened him with naked blades, and wished to lead him to the Southern Hall.
idiomatic: In the third month of the third year of the Heqing era, several dozen bandits led by Tian Zili plotted to make You their figurehead; posing as imperial envoys, they went straight to his residence, entered the inner chamber, declared an edict, dragged him onto a horse, held blades to his throat, and tried to march him toward the Southern Hall.

literal: You cried out in refusal and would not submit; he was thereupon murdered. He was thirty-two years of age; court and realm alike mourned him bitterly.
idiomatic: You shouted his refusal and would not submit; he was murdered on the spot. He was thirty-two. Court and realm mourned.

literal: Before You was seized, his consort Lady Zheng dreamed that a man cut off You's head and carried it away; she found it ominous, and within several days You was killed.
idiomatic: Before the attack, his consort Lady Zheng dreamed of a man severing You's head and carrying it away; she took it as an ill omen, and within days You was dead.

literal: He was posthumously granted the Acting Yellow Battle-Axe, Grand Preceptor, Grand Commandant, and Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing, and given an imperial mourning carriage.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted the acting yellow battle-axe, grand preceptor, grand commandant, and recorder of the Masters of Writing, with an imperial mourning carriage.

literal: His son Baode succeeded him, holding the rank of Opener of the Way and Concurrent Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: His son Baode succeeded, serving as opener of the way and concurrent left vice director of the Masters of Writing.

literal: Prince Gangsu of Shangdang, Huan, style name Jingshou, was the seventh son of Shenwu.
idiomatic: Prince Gangsu of Shangdang (Huan), whose style name was Jingshou, was the seventh son of Gao Huan.

literal: By nature he was heroic and outstanding, daring and unlike others; even in childhood he always reckoned himself destined for generalship.
idiomatic: Naturally heroic and bold, unmatched even in boyhood, he always counted himself born for command.

literal: Shenwu, impressed, loved him and said, "This boy is like me."
idiomatic: Gao Huan admired him and said, "This boy is my image."

literal: When he grew up he could lift a tripod; in talent and martial prowess he was without peer.
idiomatic: Grown to manhood he could lift a bronze tripod; in arms and valor none could match him.

literal: He often told those at his side, "A man must not be without learning — only he need not become an Erudite."
idiomatic: He often told his attendants, "A man must have learning — he need only avoid becoming a pedant."

literal: Therefore he read books and knew the outlines of things, but was not deeply devoted to study.
idiomatic: He read enough to grasp the main points, but never lost himself in books.

literal: In the Yuanxiang era he was enfeoffed Duke of Pingyuan Commandery.
idiomatic: In the Yuanxiang era he was enfeoffed Duke of Pingyuan Commandery.

literal: When Wenxiang met with assassins, Huan was still young and at the Western Academy; hearing an uproar in the palace, he started and said, "Eldest brother must have met disaster!"
idiomatic: When Gao Cheng fell to assassins, Huan was still a boy at the Western Academy; hearing uproar in the palace, he cried, "Eldest brother has met disaster!"

literal: He strung his bow and rushed out.
idiomatic: He strung his bow and ran out.

literal: At the end of the Wuding era he was appointed Governor of Ji Province and governed the province with distinction.
idiomatic: At the end of the Wuding era he was appointed governor of Ji Province and governed with distinction.

literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he was enfeoffed Prince of Shangdang and served successively as Director of the Secretariat and Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: At the opening of the Tianbao era he was enfeoffed Prince of Shangdang and rose through director of the Secretariat and left vice director of the Masters of Writing.

literal: Together with Prince of Changshan Yan and others he built fortified camps to attack the enemy.
idiomatic: With Prince of Changshan Gao Yan and others he built fortified camps for punitive raids.

literal: He then gathered rowdies beneath Ye, who harassed the commanderies and counties and were reported by the judiciary.
idiomatic: He then gathered ruffians from Ye who harassed the counties and were denounced by the judiciary.

literal: Wenxuan executed several of his attendants and reprimanded Huan as well.
idiomatic: Gao Yang executed several of his attendants and rebuked Huan himself.

literal: In the sixth year he led troops escorting Liang's Prince Xiao Ming back to Jiangnan, and also broke through Dong Pass, slaying Liang's Special Advance Pei Zhiheng and others; his fame was at its height.
idiomatic: In the sixth year he escorted Liang's Prince Xiao Ming south to Jiangnan, broke Dong Pass, and slew Liang's special advance Pei Zhiheng and others — his fame standing at its height.

literal: In the eighth year he was made Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: In the eighth year he was made recorder of the Masters of Writing.

literal: At first diviners had said that the destroyer of the Gao would wear black; hence after Shenwu, whenever they went abroad they did not wish to meet Buddhist monks, because monks wore black.
idiomatic: Diviners had once said the destroyer of the Gao would wear black; after Gao Huan's death the court on its travels avoided Buddhist monks for that reason.

literal: At that time Wenxuan was at Jinyang; following his superstition he asked those at his side, "What thing is blackest?"
idiomatic: Gao Yang was then at Jinyang; acting on this fear he asked his attendants, "What is blackest of all?"

literal: They answered, "Nothing blacker than lacquer."
idiomatic: They answered, "Nothing surpasses lacquer."

literal: The Emperor decided that Huan as the seventh son must be the omen, and sent Storehouse Commissioner Poliuhan Bosheng to Ye to summon Huan.
idiomatic: The emperor decided Huan, as the seventh son, must be the omen, and sent storehouse commissioner Poliuhan Bosheng to Ye to summon him.

literal: When Huan reached Zimo Bridge he killed Bosheng and fled; he forded a river, but local men seized him and delivered him to the Emperor.
idiomatic: At Zimo Bridge Huan killed Bosheng and fled; he forded a river, but local men seized him and delivered him to the emperor.

literal: He was placed in an iron cage and, together with Prince Jianping of Yong'an Jun, was put in an underground dungeon.
idiomatic: He was caged in iron and shut in the underground dungeon with Prince Jianping of Yong'an Jun.

literal: After more than a year he was killed together with Jun. He was twenty-six years of age.
idiomatic: After more than a year he was killed together with Jun. He was twenty-six.

literal: His consort Lady Li was given in marriage to Feng Wenluo — an old household slave of the imperial clan who through long service had risen to governor; the Emperor had ordered Wenluo and others to kill Huan, and therefore gave him Huan's wife.
idiomatic: His consort Lady Li was given to Feng Wenluo — an old household slave of the imperial clan who through long service had risen to provincial governor; the emperor had ordered Wenluo and others to kill Huan, and so gave him Huan's wife.

literal: In the first year of Qianming the scattered bones of the two princes were gathered and buried; Huan was posthumously made Minister of Works and given the posthumous name Gangsu.
idiomatic: In the first year of the Qianming era the scattered bones of both princes were gathered and buried; Huan was posthumously made minister of works with the posthumous name Gangsu.

literal: An edict ordered Lady Li to return to her residence.
idiomatic: An edict ordered Lady Li back to her own residence.

literal: Wenluo, still bearing his old grudge, dressed himself finely and came calling on Lady Li; she arrayed attendants on either side, summoned Wenluo to stand below the steps, and reproached him, saying, "Through calamity and exile I suffered the deepest shame; my resolve was too weak and I could not end my own life — by the grace of an edict I was allowed to return to my household.
idiomatic: Wenluo, still nursing his old grievance, dressed finely and came to call; Lady Li arrayed her attendants, had Wenluo stand below the steps, and upbraided him: "Cast into calamity and exile, I suffered unspeakable shame; my spirit was too weak to die, and only by grace of an edict could I return home.

literal: What sort of household slave are you, that you still dare show yourself to insult me!"
idiomatic: What household wretch are you, to dare present yourself and insult me again!"

literal: She then had him beaten a hundred strokes until blood pooled on the ground.
idiomatic: She had him beaten a hundred strokes until blood spread across the floor.

literal: Huan had no son by his principal wife; his eldest son by a concubine, Baoyan, inherited the title in the second year of Heqing, holding the ranks of Golden Chalice Grand Master of Splendor and Opener of the Way Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies.
idiomatic: Huan had no son by his principal wife; Baoyan, eldest son by a concubine, inherited in the second year of the Heqing era as golden-chalice grand master of splendor and opener of the way equal in honor to the three excellencies.

literal: Liang, style name Yandao, was by nature respectful and filial, handsome in bearing, and fond of letters.
idiomatic: Liang, styled Yandao, was respectful and filial by nature, graceful in bearing, and devoted to letters.

literal: As Governor of Xu Province he was dismissed for seizing merchants' goods.
idiomatic: Made governor of Xu Province, he was dismissed for seizing merchants' property.

literal: When Houzhu was defeated and fled to Ye, Liang followed him and was promoted to Concurrent Grand Commandant and Grand Tutor.
idiomatic: When Houzhu was defeated and fled to Ye, Liang went with him and was made concurrent grand commandant and grand tutor.

literal: When Zhou troops entered Ye, Liang held Qixia Gate in defense.
idiomatic: When Zhou troops entered Ye, Liang held Qixia Gate.

literal: Every other army fled without fighting; Zhou soldiers entered through every gate, and only then did Liang's force withdraw.
idiomatic: The other armies broke without a fight; Zhou soldiers entered every gate before Liang's troops finally withdrew.

literal: Liang entered the horse-course enclosure within the imperial temple, wept in lament and bowed his farewell, and was then seized by Zhou troops.
idiomatic: Liang entered the horse-course within the imperial temple, wept his farewell, and was then taken by Zhou troops.

literal: Taken west into Guan, he was granted the rank of Yitong by regulation, assigned to a distant frontier, and died at Long Province.
idiomatic: Taken into Guan he received the rank of yitong by regulation, was posted to a distant frontier, and died at Long Province.

literal: When Prince Yanzong of Ande proclaimed himself emperor at Jinyang, he had Liu Zi'ang draft a memorial to Hui, saying, "The sovereign has fled; the ancestral temple weighs heavily on us; the lords press us to act — we temporarily hold command, but in the end power must return to our uncle."
idiomatic: When Prince Yanzong of Ande proclaimed himself at Jinyang, he had Liu Zi'ang draft a memorial to Hui: "The sovereign has fled, the ancestral temple hangs in the balance, the lords press us to act; we hold command only for the moment — in the end it must return to Your Highness."

literal: Hui said, "I am the emperor's subject — how could I accept such a memorial?"
idiomatic: Hui said, "I am the emperor's subject — how could I accept this?"

literal: He seized Zi'ang and sent him to Ye.
idiomatic: He seized Zi'ang and sent him to Ye.

literal: When the Emperor reached Ji Province and abdicated in Hui's favor, the memorial never reached him.
idiomatic: When the emperor reached Ji Province and abdicated in Hui's favor, the memorial never reached him.

literal: Hui and Prince Xiaogong of Guangning raised more than forty thousand men in Ji Province to resist the Zhou army.
idiomatic: Hui and Prince Xiaogong of Guangning mustered more than forty thousand men in Ji Province to resist Zhou.

literal: Zhou's Prince of Qi, Yuwen Xian, came to attack and first sent letters and an amnesty edict; Hui sank them all in a well.
idiomatic: Zhou's Prince of Qi Yuwen Xian marched against them, first sending letters and an amnesty edict; Hui drowned them all in a well.

literal: Defeated in battle, Hui and Xiaogong were both captured.
idiomatic: Defeated, Hui and Xiaogong were both taken.

literal: Xian said, "Prince of Rencheng — why must it come to this?"
idiomatic: Xian said, "Prince of Rencheng — why must it end like this?"

literal: Hui said, "I am a subject-son of the Shenwu Emperor; of fifteen brothers I alone survived. To meet the dynasty's fall and die today — I need not blush before our tombs."
idiomatic: Hui said, "I am a son of Gao Huan; of fifteen brothers I alone survive. To see the altars overturned and die today — I need feel no shame before our tombs."

literal: Xian admired his spirit and returned his wife and children.
idiomatic: Xian admired his spirit and restored his wife and children.

literal: As they neared Ye city, Hui wept aloud on horseback and threw himself to the ground, blood streaming down his face.
idiomatic: Approaching Ye, Hui wept on horseback and threw himself to earth, blood covering his face.

literal: Reaching Chang'an, he soon died together with Houzhu.
idiomatic: At Chang'an he soon died together with Houzhu.

literal: His consort Lady Lu was given to Husi Zheng; disheveled and filthy, she kept long fasts and neither spoke nor smiled.
idiomatic: His consort Lady Lu was given to Husi Zheng; unkempt and mute, she kept long fasts and neither spoke nor smiled.

literal: When Zheng released her, she became a nun.
idiomatic: When Zheng released her, she took the tonsure.

literal: In the third year of Sui's Kaihuang era she petitioned Emperor Wen to bury Hui and his five sons on the north plain of Chang'an.
idiomatic: In the third year of the Kaihuang era of Sui she petitioned Emperor Wen to bury Hui and his five sons on Chang'an's north plain.

literal: Prince Kangmu of Gaoyang, Shi, was the eleventh son of Shenwu.
idiomatic: Prince Kangmu of Gaoyang (Shi) was the eleventh son of Gao Huan.

literal: He was enfeoffed in the first year of Tianbao.
idiomatic: He was enfeoffed in the first year of the Tianbao era.

literal: In the tenth year he was gradually promoted to Chief Minister of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: In the tenth year he rose to chief minister of the Masters of Writing.

literal: Because he was glib, amusing, and adept at flattery, he won Wenxuan's favor, always attended him, and walked about beating the other princes with a staff.
idiomatic: Glib, amusing, and adept at flattery, he won Gao Yang's favor, kept always at his side, and carried a staff with which he beat the other princes.

literal: The Empress Dowager deeply resented him.
idiomatic: The empress dowager bitterly resented him.

literal: His consort's father, Chief Commandant's Senior Aide Zhang Yanzi, once stopped the road to pay respects to Shi; Shi did not return the courtesy.
idiomatic: His consort's father, chief commandant's senior aide Zhang Yanzi, once intercepted the road to pay respects; Shi did not return them.

literal: When the Emperor asked why, Shi answered, "A Han man with no office — why should I show courtesy?"
idiomatic: Asked why, Shi said, "A commoner without office — why should I bow?"

literal: The Emperor thereupon promoted Yanzi to Governor of Xu Province.
idiomatic: The emperor promptly made Yanzi governor of Xu Province.

literal: When Wenxuan died Shi served concurrently as Minister of Works, led the imperial coffin, played the flute, and said, "The sovereign surely knew his servant," also beating the Hu drum for amusement.
idiomatic: When Gao Yang died Shi served as minister of works, led the coffin procession, played the flute saying "The sovereign knew me well," and beat the Hu drum for sport.

literal: The Empress Dowager had Shi beaten more than a hundred strokes; before long he died.
idiomatic: The empress dowager had him beaten more than a hundred strokes; he died shortly after.

literal: The Empress Dowager wept bitterly and said, "I feared he would never amount to anything and beat him — who dreamed he would die of his wounds!"
idiomatic: The empress dowager wept bitterly: "I feared he would never amount to anything and struck him — who dreamed the blows would kill him!"

literal: At the beginning of Qianming he was posthumously granted the Acting Yellow Battle-Axe, Grand Preceptor, Minister of Works, and Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: At the opening of the Qianming era he was posthumously granted the acting yellow battle-axe, grand preceptor, minister of works, and recorder of the Masters of Writing.

literal: His son Shiyi inherited the title.
idiomatic: His son Shiyi inherited.

literal: Prince Wenjian of Boling, Ji, was the twelfth son of Shenwu.
idiomatic: Prince Wenjian of Boling (Ji) was the twelfth son of Gao Huan.

literal: He was enfeoffed in the first year of Tianbao.
idiomatic: He was enfeoffed in the first year of the Tianbao era.

literal: Ji once accompanied Wenxuan on tour; on the road he suddenly remembered the Empress Dowager and fled back home.
idiomatic: Ji once accompanied Gao Yang on tour; on the road he suddenly missed the empress dowager and fled home.

literal: The Emperor in rage threatened him with naked blades, and from this Ji was seized with terror and confusion.
idiomatic: The emperor threatened him with naked steel; from that shock Ji was never right again.

literal: He held office through the rank of Grand Commandant.
idiomatic: He served through the rank of grand commandant.

literal: At the beginning of Heqing he was sent out as Governor of Ding Province.
idiomatic: At the opening of the Heqing era he was made governor of Ding Province.

literal: In the fifth year of Tiantong, at his post he told people, "By the count of succession my turn ought to come."
idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Tiantong era he told people at his post, "By order of succession it should be my turn next."

literal: Houzhu heard of it and secretly had him killed.
idiomatic: Houzhu heard and secretly had him killed.

literal: He was posthumously granted the Acting Yellow Battle-Axe, Grand Commandant, and Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: Posthumously granted the acting yellow battle-axe, grand commandant, and recorder of the Masters of Writing.

literal: His son Zhi inherited the title.
idiomatic: His son Zhi inherited.

literal: Prince of Fengyi, Run, style name Zize, was the fourteenth son of Shenwu.
idiomatic: Prince of Fengyi (Run), whose style name was Zize, was the fourteenth son of Gao Huan.

literal: In youth Shenwu called him "the thousand-li colt of our house."
idiomatic: In boyhood Gao Huan called him "the thousand-li colt of our house."

literal: He was enfeoffed at the beginning of Tianbao.
idiomatic: He was enfeoffed at the opening of the Tianbao era.

literal: He held office successively as Grand Mobile Headquarters of the Northeast Road, Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Area Commander, and Governor of Ding Province.
idiomatic: He served as northeast-route grand mobile headquarters, right vice director of the Masters of Writing, area commander, and governor of Ding Province.

literal: Run had handsome looks; at fourteen or fifteen his mother Consort Zheng slept with him in the same bed, and obscene sounds were heard.
idiomatic: Run was handsome; at fourteen or fifteen he shared a bed with his mother Consort Zheng, and lewd sounds were heard.

literal: When grown he was upright, cautious, and refined, skilled in official business; even in exposing hidden fraud no corrupt clerk could conceal the facts from him.
idiomatic: Grown, he was upright, cautious, and skilled in office; in exposing hidden fraud no clerk could hide from him.

literal: Opener of the Way Wang Huiluo and Six-Province Commander-in-Chief Dugu Zhi encroached on public land and accepted bribes; Run investigated and reported them.
idiomatic: Opener of the way Wang Huiluo and six-province commander-in-chief Dugu Zhi had encroached on public land and taken bribes; Run investigated and impeached them.

literal: The two submitted a memorial saying that when the prince saw off a capital envoy he climbed the old platform of Emperor Wen of Wei, looked south, and sighed — none could fathom his intent.
idiomatic: The two memorialized that when Run saw off a capital envoy he climbed Cao Pi's old platform, gazed south, and sighed — no one could read his mind.

literal: Wucheng sent Yuan Wenyao to the province with an edict, saying, "Prince of Fengyi Run has been careful from youth; at his post he has committed no wrong — I know him well.
idiomatic: Gao Zhan sent Yuan Wenyao with an edict: "Prince Run has been careful from youth and committed no crime in office — I know him thoroughly.

literal: To climb high and gaze far is human nature; vermin trying to invent slander and twist facts out of nothing."
idiomatic: To climb high and look far is only human; these vermin would invent treason out of thin air."

literal: Huiluo was sentenced to two hundred lashes; Dugu Zhi to one hundred strokes with the staff.
idiomatic: Huiluo received two hundred lashes; Dugu Zhi one hundred strokes of the staff.

literal: He soon became Chief Minister of the Masters of Writing and Concurrent Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince, and successively Minister of Works, Grand Commandant, Grand Marshal, Governor of Si Province, Grand Tutor, Grand Mobile Headquarters of the Henan Road, and Concurrent Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing; he was separately enfeoffed Duke of Wencheng Commandery, Grand Preceptor, and Grand Preceptor of the Realm — and again made Governor of Ding Province.
idiomatic: He became chief minister of the Masters of Writing and junior tutor of the crown prince, then minister of works, grand commandant, grand marshal, governor of Si Province, grand tutor, Henan-route grand mobile headquarters, and recorder of the Masters of Writing; he was separately enfeoffed duke of Wencheng, grand preceptor and grand preceptor of the realm — and again made governor of Ding Province.

literal: At his death he was posthumously granted the Acting Yellow Battle-Axe and Left Chancellor.
idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously granted the acting yellow battle-axe and left chancellor.

literal: His son Maode succeeded.
idiomatic: His son Maode succeeded.

literal: Prince Jinghuai of Hanyang, Qia, style name Jingyan, was the fifteenth son of Shenwu.
idiomatic: Prince Jinghuai of Hanyang (Qia), whose style name was Jingyan, was the fifteenth son of Gao Huan.

literal: He was enfeoffed in the first year of Tianbao.
idiomatic: He was enfeoffed in the first year of the Tianbao era.

literal: In the fifth year he died, aged thirteen.
idiomatic: In the fifth year he died, aged thirteen.

literal: In the first year of Qianming he was posthumously made Grand Tutor and Minister of Works.
idiomatic: In the first year of the Qianming era he was posthumously made grand tutor and minister of works.

literal: Having no sons, the second son of the Prince of Rencheng, Jiande, was made his heir.
idiomatic: Having no son, Jiande, second son of the Prince of Rencheng, was made his heir.
